public_rationale: On Nov 20, 2024, three days before the post, Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang said on stage that 'the wall has been the topic du jour for the past few weeks' and answered 'yes and no' to whether AI had hit a wall. The Verge's report of that summit said Google and others were seeing diminishing returns, and its subhead said everyone in AI seemed to agree models were hitting a scaling wall. A report dated Nov 6 quotes Marc Andreessen saying models were 'hitting the same ceiling on capabilities', which is the diminishing-returns idea. Together, the named people and others used the wall framing and the diminishing-returns idea in roughly the weeks before the post. One caveat: Andreessen's remarks fall about 17 days before the post, and he said 'ceiling', not 'wall'.
limitations: Andreessen did not use the exact phrase 'hitting a wall'; the claim is scored on the group reading.
Andreessen's remarks fall at the loose edge of 'last couple weeks'.
News reports are used rather than the original recordings.

'Many other tech CEOs and others' is satisfied by the two named people plus reporting that the wall idea was widely held in the industry in that window.
criteria.support_condition: Dated reports from about 2–23 November 2024 show Wang and Andreessen publicly saying that scaling or capabilities were hitting a wall, ceiling, or diminishing returns, and that this view was widely shared among industry leaders.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that Wang and Andreessen did not express such views in that window, or that they explicitly rejected the wall or diminishing-returns idea at that time.

evidence.excerpt: “The wall has been the topic du jour for the past few weeks,” Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang, whose company helps OpenAI, Meta, and others train their models, told the conference’s host, Eric Newcomer, during the morning’s first session. “Have we hit a wall? Yes and no.”
evidence.explanation: Wang publicly used the 'wall' framing on Nov 20, 2024, three days before the post. He partly agreed that a wall had been hit, and the report links it to diminishing returns from training.

evidence.excerpt: Google and others are starting to see diminishing returns from training their next models.
evidence.explanation: Shows the diminishing-returns idea was in wide circulation across the industry in November 2024. The article's subhead says 'Everyone in AI seems to agree that new models are hitting a scaling wall.'

evidence.excerpt: “They’re kind of hitting the same ceiling on capabilities. Now there’s lots of smart people in the industry working to break through those ceilings, but sitting here today, if you just looked at the data, if you just looked at the charts of performance over time, what you would say is there’s at least a local topping out of capabilities that’s happening,” Andreessen continued.
evidence.explanation: Andreessen voiced the idea of diminishing returns, a ceiling and a topping out of capabilities, in podcast remarks reported Nov 6, 2024. He did not use the word 'wall'. The event date is the report's publication date; the remarks were made on or shortly before it.
